findings.english_quote: Countenance renders opsis, also face or appearance.
findings.issue: Footnote a describes the standard edition’s rendering rather than the simplified edition’s actual choice, “face.” This leaves the reader-facing explanation of the selected English word inaccurate, although “face” itself faithfully renders the source here.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed correction for fresh review: “Face renders opsis, also appearance or countenance.” Retain the subsequent disclosure of the contrast and reported witness evidence.

summary: Both editions were independently checked against every clause of the selected Greek. Their main texts preserve the age contrast, both causes of despair, exclusive expectation of death, inheritance and posture sequence, corruption from former deeds, singular versus plural spirits, past actions, the Lord’s joy, and the whole-heart communal-peace condition for further disclosure. The standard edition is accepted within this review’s scope; the simplified edition needs a minor footnote correction. The witness notes are consistent with the supplied attributed reports and distinguish editorial supplies, corrections, and differing readings without replacing the working source. This assessment does not authenticate unseen manuscripts or certify exhaustive collation.
